topics.title: Intersecting lines: linear pairs and vertically opposite angles

concepts.learning_objective: Use the fact that a linear pair formed by two intersecting lines adds up to 180° to find unknown angles.
Identify vertically opposite angles and reason why they are always equal.
Explain why measured angles may differ slightly from values found by geometric reasoning.
Recognise perpendicular lines as intersecting lines that form four right angles.
Describe parallel lines as lines in the same plane that never meet however far they are extended.

topics.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines in paper folding; notation

concepts.learning_objective: Identify and count parallel and perpendicular creases formed by folding a square sheet.
Read and use arrow marks for parallel lines and the square mark for perpendicular lines.
Describe the eight angles formed when a transversal cuts two lines and the number of distinct measures possible.
Use equality of corresponding angles to find angles and to decide whether two lines are parallel.
Draw parallel lines with a ruler and set square and justify them using equal corresponding angles.
Make a line parallel to a given line through a point by folding two perpendiculars, and justify it.
Find alternate angles formed by a transversal on parallel lines and justify that they are equal.
Use the fact that interior angles on the same side of a transversal on parallel lines add up to 180°.
